fields.text: Sing, from awesome-noodles (github.com/nanoodlecom/awesome-noodles), set up for hires in plain words: the brief is the song idea, and an optional line "Style: ..." sets the Style input (for example: 80s trip-hop bands that have a female singer and an awesome electric style). The original's "Preferred bands" input is this Style input. An optional line "Duration: ..." sets the target length. MiniMax Music 3 takes no length setting, so the length is steered through the amount of lyrics and the arrangement prompt and is approximate. Three text calls write lyrics, arrange them and name what would clash; MiniMax Music 3 sings the result. Outputs: the song (mp3) and the lyrics.
No style given. Choose a style that fits the song idea.

fields.system: Write original, singable lyrics from the song idea and the requested style. Size the lyrics to the target length at about 1.1 words per second of song, never more than 280 words: about 60 seconds is one short verse and one chorus (about 65 words); about 120 seconds is about 130 words; about 180 seconds is about 200 words; about 240 seconds is about 260 words. Use concrete images, an emotional point of view, natural stresses and short lines that fit the requested mood. Build one memorable hook and repeat it in each chorus. Let the style inform rhythm and atmosphere; never name a band or artist, quote their songs or copy a recognizable lyric. For 150 seconds or more use [Verse 1], [Chorus], [Verse 2], [Chorus], [Bridge], [Chorus], [Outro]; for a shorter song drop sections from the end and keep at least one verse and one chorus. Output only the section labels and lyrics.

Write one compact music-generator prompt: a single paragraph, at most 70 words and 500 characters. Say the target length once, in seconds (for example: about 150 seconds long). Use the supplied idea, style and finished lyrics to choose tempo, groove, drum texture, bass, instruments and vocal delivery. If the style names artists, translate them into descriptions of sound; do not name artists or songs. Keep the requested genre and mood. No section-by-section plan, headings, lyrics or commentary. Output only the compact arrangement.

Read the actual arrangement. Name exactly three specific musical choices that would undermine its groove, instruments, vocal delivery or mood. Never reject a requested element. Output only three short comma-separated phrases, at most 20 words and 120 characters total. No artist names, explanations or generic quality complaints.
